---
title: "Commuter Friction Survey – Data Cleaning"
author: "Group Project – Data Analysis and Preparation of Reports"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## 1. Load packages

Run this once in the Console first if the packages are not installed:
`install.packages(c("readxl", "dplyr", "writexl", "knitr", "rmarkdown"))`

```{r packages}
library(readxl)   # read the Excel file
library(dplyr)    # data cleaning
library(writexl)  # write the cleaned Excel file
library(knitr)    # nice tables in the report
```

## 2. Read the raw data

The Excel file must be in the **same folder** as this `.Rmd` file.

```{r read}
raw <- read_excel("commuter-survey-complete.xlsx",
                  sheet = "Data (labels)")

dim(raw)   # rows, columns
```

## 3. Keep only students staying at home or a relative's home

This must be done **before** removing the A6 column, because the filter uses A6.
"Other (please specify)" is the one respondent who stays at a relative's home.

```{r filter}
a6 <- "A6 Where do you stay during the semester?"

kable(count(raw, .data[[a6]]), caption = "A6 before filtering")

data <- raw %>%
  filter(.data[[a6]] %in% c("Home", "Other (please specify)"))

nrow(data)   # respondents kept
```

## 4. Remove unwanted columns

Removes ID, Submitted, Status, Language, Duration (s), A1, index and both A6
columns (the A6 question and its "other (specify)" text).

```{r remove}
data <- data %>%
  select(-ID, -Submitted, -Status, -Language, -`Duration (s)`,
         -starts_with("A1 "),
         -starts_with("index "),
         -starts_with("A6 "))

names(data)
```

## 5. Faculty (A3): keep the top 5, merge the rest

The top 5 are worked out from the filtered data.

```{r faculty}
a3 <- "A3 Your faculty"

kable(count(data, .data[[a3]], sort = TRUE), caption = "A3 before merging")

top5 <- data %>%
  count(.data[[a3]], sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  pull(1)

data[[a3]] <- ifelse(data[[a3]] %in% top5, data[[a3]], "Other faculties")

kable(count(data, .data[[a3]], sort = TRUE), caption = "A3 after merging")
```

## 6. Vehicle changes (B3): relabel as text categories

B3 mixes numbers (0, 1, 2) with text ("3 or more"), so Excel flags the numbers
as "Number stored as text". B3 is a categorical variable, so it is relabelled
with clear text labels.

```{r b3}
b3 <- names(data)[startsWith(names(data), "B3 ")]

data[[b3]] <- recode(as.character(data[[b3]]),
                     "0"         = "No change",
                     "1"         = "1 change",
                     "2"         = "2 changes",
                     "3 or more" = "3 or more changes")

kable(count(data, .data[[b3]]), caption = "B3 after relabelling")
```

## 7. Rename columns with short, meaningful names

Each long question heading is replaced with a short name. The table below is the
variable key, which is also saved as a second sheet in the Excel file.

```{r rename}
new_names <- c(
  A2  = "days_per_week",      # Days per week travelling to university
  A3  = "faculty",            # Faculty
  A4  = "study_year",         # Year of study
  A5  = "gender",             # Gender
  B1  = "distance",           # One-way distance to university
  B2  = "main_mode",          # Main transport mode
  B3  = "vehicle_changes",    # Number of vehicle changes
  B4  = "access_mode",        # How they get to the main vehicle
  B5  = "egress_mode",        # How they get from main vehicle to the gate
  B6  = "seat",               # Usually get a seat or stand
  B7  = "late_arrivals",      # Days per week arriving 15+ min late
  B8  = "trip_time",          # One-way trip time
  B9  = "wait_time",          # Waiting time for vehicle
  B10 = "departure_time",     # Time leaving for university
  B11 = "travel_budget",      # Share of daily budget spent on travel
  B12 = "feel_unsafe",        # How often they feel unsafe
  C1  = "stressed_relaxed",   # Stressed (-3) to relaxed (+3)
  C2  = "worried_confident",  # Worried (-3) to confident (+3)
  C3  = "hurried_calm",       # Hurried (-3) to calm (+3)
  C4  = "stress_these_days",  # Feel this kind of stress these days
  D1  = "sleep_quality",      # Sleep quality last night
  D2  = "workload_pressure",  # Academic workload pressure today
  D3  = "crowding",           # Crowding on bus/train today
  D4  = "weather_impact"      # Weather made commute harder today
)

# The question code is the first word of each heading (e.g. "B3")
old_headings <- names(data)
codes        <- sub(" .*", "", old_headings)

variable_key <- data.frame(
  variable = unname(new_names[codes]),
  code     = codes,
  question = sub("^\\S+ ", "", old_headings)
)

names(data) <- new_names[codes]

kable(variable_key, caption = "Variable key")
```

## 8. Commute Stress Score (STS) and stress level

Based on the STS Stress Score Guide:

* C1–C3 are scored from −3 to +3. The number is taken from the start of each
  label (e.g. "-2 Quite stressed" → −2, "+1 Slightly relaxed" → +1).
* **Stress score = − (C1 + C2 + C3) / 3**, ranging from −3 (very relaxed) to
  +3 (very stressed). A higher value means more stress.
* **Stress level:** above +1 = High, −1 to +1 = Moderate, below −1 = Low.

```{r stress}
# Take the leading number from each label, e.g. "-2 Quite stressed" -> -2
score_of <- function(x) as.numeric(sub(" .*", "", x))

c1 <- score_of(data$stressed_relaxed)
c2 <- score_of(data$worried_confident)
c3 <- score_of(data$hurried_calm)

raw_score <- -(c1 + c2 + c3) / 3

data$stress_score <- round(raw_score, 2)
data$stress_level <- case_when(
  raw_score >  1 ~ "High",
  raw_score < -1 ~ "Low",
  TRUE           ~ "Moderate"     # -1 to +1, including exactly -1 and +1
)

# Check against the worked examples in the guide (A = +2.00 High,
# B = 0.00 Moderate, C = -2.33 Low)
ex <- data.frame(C1 = c(-2, 1, 3), C2 = c(-1, 0, 2), C3 = c(-3, -1, 2))
ex$score <- round(-(ex$C1 + ex$C2 + ex$C3) / 3, 2)
kable(ex, caption = "Worked examples from the guide")

# Add the two new variables to the variable key
variable_key <- rbind(
  variable_key,
  data.frame(variable = c("stress_score", "stress_level"),
             code     = c("STS", "STS"),
             question = c("Commute Stress Score = -(C1 + C2 + C3) / 3, from -3 (very relaxed) to +3 (very stressed)",
                          "Stress level: High (score above +1), Moderate (-1 to +1), Low (below -1)"))
)

summary(data$stress_score)
kable(count(data, stress_level), caption = "Stress level")
```

## 9. Save the cleaned data

```{r save}
write_xlsx(list("Cleaned data" = data, "Variable key" = variable_key),
           "commuter-survey-cleaned.xlsx")
```

The cleaned file **commuter-survey-cleaned.xlsx** is saved in the same folder as
this `.Rmd` file: `r nrow(data)` respondents and `r ncol(data)` variables.
It has two sheets: **Cleaned data** and **Variable key**.
